blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—The upcoming closed fishing season in major fishing grounds across the country could trigger an artificial shortage of fish and drive up market prices, the fishers’ group Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas (Pamalakaya) warned. In a statement, Pamalakaya said the annual three-month fishing ban, scheduled across several fishing grounds between November and February next year, could disrupt local fish production and supply while cutting the income of affected fishing communities. The closures cover major fishing grounds, including the Visayan Sea, Zamboanga Peninsula, Palawan, Balayan Bay in Batangas and Tayabas Bay in Quezon. READ: ‘Tamban’ closed fishing season in […]...
